radiusSource: Radius 28.216 (26.180 to 30.502) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 19,629,649 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 4.198 (4.088 to 4.238) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4532 +/- 20.8 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 6508444357750002176: teff_gspphot 4532.2305 K (16th-84th percentiles 4510.128-4551.6943), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 6508444357750002176: teff_gspphot 4532.2305 K (16th-84th percentiles 4510.128-4551.6943), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gaia-dr3-6508444357750002176.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.160, rounded to two decimals
